caption: Session
description: The Session object describes details about an authenticated session. e.g. Session Creation Time, Session Issuer.
name: session

count.description: The number of identical sessions spawned from the same source IP, destination IP, application, and content/threat type seen over a period of time.

created_time.description: The time when the session was created.

expiration_reason.description: The reason which triggered the session expiration.

is_elevated.description: Indicates whether the session runs with elevated privileges, for example a logon session that holds full administrative rights instead of a filtered set of rights.

references.description: Security event 4624, An account was successfully logged on (Elevated Token field)

is_restricted_admin.description: Indicates whether the remote interactive logon that created the session used restricted admin mode, in which the client authenticates without sending reusable credentials to the remote host, so they cannot be harvested there. It is only meaningful for remote interactive logons. Because restricted admin mode also lets a client log on with an NTLM hash instead of a password, a restricted admin logon from an unexpected account or host is worth reviewing.

references.description: Security event 4624, An account was successfully logged on (Restricted Admin Mode field)
Remote Desktop Protocol: Basic Connectivity and Graphics Remoting, 2.2.1.2.1 RDP Negotiation Response (RESTRICTED_ADMIN_MODE_SUPPORTED)

issuer.description: The identifier of the session issuer.

terminal.description: The Pseudo Terminal associated with the session. Ex: the tty or pts value.

uid.description: The unique identifier of the session.

uid_alt.description: The alternate unique identifier of the session. e.g. AWS ARN - arn:aws:sts::123344444444:assumed-role/Admin/example-session.

uuid.description: The universally unique identifier of the session.
